native_result.query: How were the phases of the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) characterized in terms of the first principal component in a PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices?
native_result.HypoA: During the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE), both phases are primarily associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: In a PCA on the forms of capital performed on hundred-year time slices (capital.csv, BCE 500-4300, 12 interpolated Z variables), PC1 (30.3% of variance; oriented with CopperGold positive, loading +0.41) contrasts valuable/prestige accumulation - CopperGold, PotteryDecoration, Depot, HatchetSword, Dagger, MonumentSize, HouseSize, MonumentCount (positive loadings) - against PotteryForm, AxesCelts, Amber, Sickle (negative loadings). Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE): PC1 strongly and steadily negative - all 5 century-slices <0, mean ~ -1.37 (~0.7 SD below series mean), declining from ~ -0.58 (3400 BCE) to ~ -1.78 (3000 BCE), a deepening trough in capital accumulation. Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE): PC1 still negative (all 7 slices <0, mean ~ -1.12) but rising, recovering from ~ -1.50 (2900 BCE) to ~ -0.41 (2300 BCE) toward the series mean - gradual renewed accumulation (led by social capital: CopperGold/MonumentCount turning positive) without reaching the positive range.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Parse capital.csv (comma-decimals), drop group/color; 39 hundred-year slices BCE 500-4300. 2) Define phases by group column: MN=BCE 3400-3000 (5 slices), Younger Neolithic=BCE 2900-2300 (7 slices). 3) Correlation-matrix PCA on 12 capital variables -> overall PC1; per-capital PCAs using corrected mapping (Symbolic=HatchetSword+Dagger+HouseSize; Social=CopperGold+Amber+MonumentCount; Cultural=PotteryForm+PotteryDecoration; Economic=Depot+Sickle+AxesCelts+MonumentSize). 4) Orient PC1 signs by dominant loading (+). 5) Per phase compute mean, min/max, fraction negative, first/last, OLS slope per 100 BCE, r2; compare vs full-series mean (0, sigma=1.908). 6) Optional context: correlation of overall PC1 with pollen openness (r~0.71-0.73).
